content: Enterocolitis, also referred to as coloenteritis, is a medical condition characterized by inflammation affecting both the colon and the small intestine. However, in most cases, the inflammation is classified as either of the following: Enteritis: This term specifically refers to inflammation localized to the small intestine. Colitis: This term describes inflammation of the large intestine, with a particular focus on the colon. Types of Enterocolitis There are several distinct forms of enterocolitis, including: Necrotizing Enterocolitis: This is a severe and potentially life-threatening condition that predominantly affects premature infants. Autistic Enterocolitis: A controversial and debated condition that has been described as a bowel disease occurring in children with autism. Pseudomembranous Enterocolitis: Also known as Pseudomembranous Colitis, this condition is characterized by the presence of pseudomembranes in the colon, often associated with Clostridioides difficile infection. Causes of Enterocolitis Certain medications and substances have been identified as potential causes of enterocolitis, including: Ipilimumab: An immune checkpoint inhibitor used in cancer immunotherapy, which can lead to immune-mediated colitis as a side effect. Ixabepilone: A chemotherapeutic agent that may induce gastrointestinal inflammation as an adverse reaction. Tetracyclines: A class of antibiotics, including drugs such as idarubicin hydrochloride, which can cause gastrointestinal irritation and inflammation in some cases.
